turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a call at 4:40, so I'll be brief. Owen found out about a zero from the gradebook on his phone, in the middle of class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that?
I didn't come for pleasantries, Hale. I asked you a question: who decided to enter that zero, and why wasn't I called first?
Can you read me your notes word for word?
You're asking to see my notes? You'll have my position in writing. What I'll read you is your own school's procedure 4.2: the parent is contacted before any mark is entered, and nobody called me.
Not those notes. Your instructions. What were you told to do in this meeting?
Told by whom? Nobody tells me what to do, Hale. I'm here about Owen's zero, so answer my question: who decided to enter it before anyone called me?
What do you plan to say if I bring up your daughter?

You'll want to be very careful about the next sentence, Hale. My daughter has nothing to do with Owen's zero, and I don't discuss my plans with the person who entered it. Answer the question, or I'll take it to the principal's office.
